messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Question about colext
parts:
Hi Miguel,

Thanks for providing the example -- that is always helpful. Unfortunately you cannot fix parameters in unmarked yet. However, if the population is closed during the first two primary periods, you could treat them as one primary period. In your example, this would mean that you need J=6 and T=3. Here is a modified version.

n <- 50 # number of sites
T <- 3 # number of primary periods
J <- 6 # number of secondary periods

site <- factor(1:50) # perhaps not wise
pp <- data.frame(matrix(c('A','B','C'), n, T, byrow=TRUE))
occasions <- data.frame(matrix(as.character(rep(1:(J*T), each=n)), n, J*T))

y <- matrix(0:1, n, J*T, byrow=TRUE)

nodataCols <- c(10:12, 16:18)
y[,nodataCols] <- occasions[,nodataCols] <- NA

umf <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=y,
siteCovs = data.frame(site=site),
obsCovs=list(occasion=occasions),
yearlySiteCovs=list(primaryPeriod=pp),
numPrimary=T)

summary(umf)


colext(~1, ~primaryPeriod, ~1, ~occasion, umf, )

Richard

Hello Unmarked users:

I am running some exploratory analysis with colext, and I am
interested in calculating colonization and extinction probabilities
for each site. However, in some models I will like to force some
colonizations and extinctions to be 0.

For example:

n <- 50 # number of sites
T <- 4 # number of primary periods
J <- 3 # number of secondary periods

site <- 1:50
years <- data.frame(matrix(rep(2010:2013, each=n), n, T))
years <- data.frame(lapply(years, as.factor))
occasions <- data.frame(matrix(rep(1:(J*T), each=n), n, J*T))

y <- matrix(0:1, n, J*T)

umf <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=y,
siteCovs = data.frame(site=site),
obsCovs=list(occasion=occasions),
yearlySiteCovs=data.frame(year=years),
numPrimary=T)

print(years)

Here I will like to build a model that forces all col and ext to be 0
between 2010 and 2011 but still calculate col/ext's between 2011-2012
and 2012-2013.

Like always any help will be greatly appreciated.
Thank you
